newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS-EU would decide Swedish EMU opt-out - Santer.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-EU would decide Swedish EMU opt-out - Santer.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer said on Wednesday it would be up to European Union leaders to decide whether Sweden could opt out of economic and monetary union (EMU) if it qualified.
"It's up to heads of state and government to take this decision," Santer said when asked at a news conference about whether Sweden has a right not to join EMU.

Sweden's ruling Social Democratic Party's executive committee ruled on Tuesday that Sweden would not join EMU at its planned launch in 1999 but kept the door open for joining before parliamentary elections due in 2002.
"I don't concern myself with what happens within political parties or domestic politics," Santer said, adding that he is only concerned with dealing with governments.
Santer said that he was confident EMU would go ahead with or without Sweden.
Sweden maintains it has a right to opt out from EMU because of a unilateral declaration it made on entry into the EU in 1995.

However, the Maastricht treaty, which Sweden adopted when it became an EU member only gives formal opt outs to Britain, which can decide, and Denmark which has already said it will not adopt the new currency.
The issue is a sensitive one because it involves an EU country deciding unilaterally not to do something it has already agreed to do on paper.

The Dutch finance ministry earlier said Sweden did not have the right under the Maastricht Treaty to opt out. But it made clear that was only the opinion of the ministry, not of the Dutch EU presidency.
It is considered highly unlikely that the EU would try to force a country to adopt the single currency if its government did not want it.
